root_sensitive_lines.text: A Subject Path is a full canonical expression identifying one thing or topic addressed by GOVERNS or DEPENDS_ON. Entity is the canonical expression root under CA-R-2462; this Definition does not enumerate a closed root-branch set. A source path retains the declared operators and full qualification; a short display label is not another identity or alias.

A path may address classification without declaring an Entity kind. `Atom.Header.Role` addresses the relative Property, while `Atom/(.Header.Role: Plan)` identifies a qualified Atom inheriting applicable Atom features and constraints. Neither form invents an intermediate Entity kind. The root and operators follow the adopted Entity syntax under CA-R-1931; no Project-name namespace layer is introduced.

**every** entity represented **in** the Subject Graph **and** **every** declared Relation Type entity **must** have **`=1`** complete canonical name formed from reusable Terms **and** any applicable registered qualification syntax **and** used exactly **in** **every** authored occurrence that mentions it. **every** such complete name **must** identify **`=1`** entity, distinct complete names **must not** identify the same entity, **and** the same complete name **must not** identify distinct entities. Outside `Term`, the complete canonical name **must** be the full admitted expression, **not** a single registered Term; the Subject root `Entity` is the sole exception.

review_lines.text: - use full Entity expressions `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package`, `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package/Eval Package`, and `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package/Runtime Package` with one consistent reusable Term `Package`; use `Entity/Object/Continuant/Structural Unit/Scope Unit` and `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module <+ Code Unit` with one consistent reusable Term `Unit`. A short complete expression, including one Term spelling, is accepted only when its exact use is source-admitted and unambiguous; being a reusable Term alone does not establish a complete name.

- use `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package`, `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module`, and `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module <+ Code Unit`: three connected entities with their three full expressions in graph Subjects and all authored mentions. Calling the same Module entity `component` merely for stylistic variation fails; a separately defined Component entity stays distinct.

`Entity/Object/Continuant/Package`, `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module`, and `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module <+ Code Unit` identify three entities. Operators, delimiters and selector syntax are not Terms. Under CA-R-1325, a complete composite Subject Expression is not one lexical Term; this does not prohibit an explicitly admitted qualified Entity expression. A short complete expression, including one Term spelling, is accepted only when its exact use is source-admitted and unambiguous; being a reusable Term alone does not establish a complete name. Parsing an arbitrary composite expression does not automatically establish a complete Entity expression or another Entity. The three-target chain introduces no fourth Entity or fourth complete expression. Naming checks must not reify component labels or shared words into new graph entities. The respective ID Properties distinguished by the contextual topic/code spellings `atom.id` and `projection.id` stay distinct and retain the explicitly defined ID meaning; these spellings do not substitute for full admitted Subject expressions. An Atom Content Role/Type expression requires independent source admission of both exact values. A Term occurrence is checked against its dedicated Term Definition, not inferred agreement of other fields.
